summary: Extensions, split view, and a lighter, quieter web.

highlights.title: Split View
highlights.body: Drag a tab onto the page to open it beside the one you're reading. Separate them again from the View menu.

highlights.title: Extensions from the Chrome Web Store
highlights.body: The store's own button now says “Add to Pulse”. Run an extension's actions and popups from the puzzle button or the command bar.

highlights.title: Ads and Trackers Blocked
highlights.body: Pulse blocks them with EasyList and EasyPrivacy. To allow them on a site, use the site controls in the address bar.

highlights.title: Tabs That Sleep
highlights.body: Tabs you haven't looked at in an hour go to sleep to free memory, and wake up right where you left them. Choose the delay in Settings.

improvements: Private windows keep nothing once you close them.
Tabs playing audio show it, and you can mute them with ⌃M.
Spaces can have an emoji icon, and you can reorder them by dragging.
Drag a tab onto a space's dot to move it there.
Swiping between spaces follows your fingers.
The empty command bar suggests recent tabs and pages.
A new sidebar bottom bar creates tabs, spaces and more.
Unpin a pinned tab from its hover button.
Help › Report a Problem… opens a bug report with diagnostics attached.
fixes: ⌘W closes the tab, not the window, even while a page has focus.
Shared screens stay sharp and smooth in video calls.
Background requests, JavaScript dialogs and camera and microphone prompts are more private.
